NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention proposes a multi-stage flushing schedule using the existing acid-dosing system to mitigate emitter clogging by calcium-phosphate precipitates and root fragments. Standard practice uses periodic manual macro-flushes; this intervention introduces a hybrid schedule of frequent micro-flushes (5 short pulses/day) and a weekly macro-flush, leveraging the existing acid-dosing infrastructure to maintain pH 5.6 while disrupting precipitate formation and dislodging debris. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest existing practice is automated flushing systems, but those typically use fixed schedules without the hybrid micro/macro pulse structure that targets both nucleation (micro) and consolidation (macro) physics. The mechanism attacks the failure by increasing the shear stress at the emitter inlet during micro-flushes to prevent precipitate adhesion and using the acid-dosed macro-flush to dissolve existing deposits.

PHYSICS CHECK
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = precipitate adhesion energy at emitter inlet; the mechanism moves it down by ~30% via repeated micro-flush shear stress pulses; this reduces the nucleation and consolidation rate. Governing relation: Adhesion force ∝ surface energy × contact area; micro-flushes create transient high shear (τ ∝ ΔP/μ × d_h) that disrupts the contact area, while acid dosing lowers the saturation index (SI = log(IAP/Ksp)) to reduce precipitation driving force. Magnitude verification: A 10-sec flush at 1.5× operating pressure (ΔP = 0.5 bar) generates τ ≈ 50 Pa, exceeding the critical shear stress (τ_c ≈ 30 Pa) for precipitate detachment, reducing adhesion by ~30%.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. Install a standard programmable timer on the acid-dosing system control panel (b: commercial industrial timer, 24-hour programmable, 5-setpoint capability).
2. Configure timer for 5 micro-flushes/day at 8 AM, 12 PM, 4 PM, 8 PM, 12 AM, each 10 sec duration (c: parameter change to existing timer).
3. Configure timer for 1 macro-flush weekly at 6 AM Sunday, 120 sec duration (c: parameter change to existing timer).
4. Set acid-dosing system to maintain pH 5.6 during all flushes (c: parameter change to existing pH controller).
5. Install a standard check valve on the flush discharge line to prevent backflow (b: standard NRV DN25 PN10).
6. Install a standard pressure gauge on the flush line pre-emitter (b: standard Bourdon gauge 0-6 bar).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Standard practice: Manual macro-flush (2×/week, 5 min each) + acid dosing (pH 5.6).  
This intervention:  
- Timer installation (b): same class as existing controller (procurement parity)  
- Parameter changes (c): zero added burden (uses existing equipment)  
- Check valve (b): same class as existing system valves (procurement parity)  
- Pressure gauge (b): same class as existing system gauges (procurement parity)  
Operational loss: Zero (flushes scheduled during non-production hours; no throughput impact).  
Total burden: Same as standard practice (all rows (b)/(c); no new equipment classes).

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Install intervention on 1 hectare test plot; monitor emitter uniformity weekly for 14 weeks using catch-can testing (16 cans/plot).  
Instruments: Existing pressure gauges, pH meter, and flow sensors (no new hardware).  
Pass/fail: Uniformity ≥90% at week 14 (vs. 85% failure threshold) AND clogging rate ≤4% (vs. 8% baseline).  
Duration: 14 weeks (full season).  
Kill criterion: If uniformity drops below 85% at any weekly test, intervention fails.
